issues.display_title: Issue #4260: [Integration] Photographer Services: replace localStorage mock with real Professional-Services API
issues.main_description_html:
Context

The Photographer "Services" page on design/photographer-professional-services is currently a UI-only slice backed by localStorage (see src/pages/Photographer/hooks/usePhotographerServices.jsx, which explicitly marks MOCK DATA and has a TODO(integration) to swap it for a real API). This task wires it to the real backend through the new proxy.

Current model (dashboard)

Each row: { id, name, url, icon } — ordered by array position. Save is row-level (handleSaveRow writes one row to localStorage); delete also row-level.

Target upstream API (Go gothru-maps-backend-go, proxied via GoThru API New)

  • GET /v1/photographers/{gothruUserId}/professional-services
    200 → { data: { professionalServices: [ {id:int, icon, name, link, order:int} ] } }
    404 → { data: { error: "Photographer not found" } }
  • PUT /v1/photographers/{gothruUserId}/professional-services
    Body → { services: [ {icon, name, link} ] } (full replace of the whole array)
    200 → { data: { message: "...", professionalServices: [...] } }
    400 on validation/role (≤20 items; name required ≤150; icon optional ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,100}$; link optional absolute http(s) ≤2048; role must be image_processing).

Mapping

Dashboard API Note
name name same
url link rename on read/write
icon icon lucide names already match regex
id (string svc-…) id (int) use API id; track new rows locally before save
position order derived from array index on save

Requirements

  1. Replace loadStoredServices / saveStoredServices (localStorage) with real API calls through the proxy:
    • Load: GET → map items to {id, name, url: link, icon}.
    • Persist: PUT with the full { services: [...] } replace semantics — rework handleSaveRow / handleDeleteRow so that save/delete edit the in-memory list, then send the whole array in one PUT (the upstream replace has no per-row endpoint).
  2. Map icon/name/link and derive order from array index.
  3. Handle loading and error states; relay upstream 404 (photographer not found) and 400 (validation/role) errors to the user via the existing toast pattern.
  4. Keep the icon picker and autocomplete catalog as-is.

Out of scope

  • No creation/modification of the upstream API — it already exists.
  • Backend/proxy tasks live on the API repo (GET proxy #1858, PUT proxy #1859 on GoThruMedia/GoThru-API-New).

Acceptance criteria

  • Opening the page loads existing professional services from the API (not localStorage).
  • Saving/deleting an item sends a single PUT with the full services array and reflects the returned list.
  • id/order are respected; url maps to API link and back.
  • Upstream error (404 / 400) is surfaced gracefully.
  • localStorage mock code is removed.

Related

  • Feature branch: design/photographer-professional-services
  • Hook to change: src/pages/Photographer/hooks/usePhotographerServices.jsx
  • Upstream endpoints: gothru-maps-backend-go src/action/v1/photographers/professionalServices.go

Result

Implemented and verified in PR: #4261

Changes

  • API Integration: Replaced localStorage mock in src/pages/Photographer/hooks/usePhotographerServices.jsx with real endpoints:
    • GET /photographers/professional-services via useLazyFetch
    • PUT /photographers/professional-services via usePut (whole-array replace semantics)
  • Field & Contract Mapping:
    • Internal url maps to API link
    • Internal icon, name, and numeric id mapped
    • Order preserved via array order
  • Status Synchronization: Redux SET_PHOTOGRAPHER dispatches status 1 if photographer was approved (status 3) per upstream business rules.
  • UI Enhancements:
    • Added NextUI Spinner on PhotographerServices.jsx during initial fetch
    • Disabled Add button during loading
    • Wired isDeleting loading indicator into DeleteModal

Ref: GoThruMedia/GoThru-API-New#1834, GoThruMedia/gothru-rag#16, GoThruMedia/frontend-rag-system

Summary

Migrate and integrate the new RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) copilot backend into the GoThru Dashboard chat widget.

Previously, the chat widget connected to the legacy session-based gpt backend (https://gpt.gothru.co). With the introduction of the gothru-rag microservice and its authenticated proxy endpoint in GoThru-API-New (POST /copilot/chat, PR #1834), the chat widget assets and dashboard integration need to be updated to consume the new RAG service with conversational context history and verified knowledge source references.

Technical Context & Scope

1. Update Static Widget Bundle (public/scripts/widget.js, public/styles/widget.css)

  • Synchronize and update the prebuilt distribution assets from GoThruMedia/frontend-rag-system (branch feat/gothru-rag-integration):
    • Point API communication to the GoThru API Copilot proxy endpoint (/copilot/chat).
    • Adapt chat request payload to include prompt message and conversation history context ({ message, context: { history }, provider }).
    • Render RAG response structure including markdown answer and referenced knowledge sources.
    • Apply updated Tailwind CSS v4 styling rules in public/styles/widget.css.

2. Cache Busting & Asset Loading (src/components/layouts/Layout.jsx, public/index.html)

  • Update version query parameters on script and stylesheet links to prevent client-side browser caching:
    • In Layout.jsx: increment /scripts/widget.js?t=v5 to /scripts/widget.js?t=v6.
    • In public/index.html: increment %PUBLIC_URL%/styles/widget.css?t=v4 to %PUBLIC_URL%/styles/widget.css?t=v6.

3. Container & Auth Handshake (#chat-container)

    • data-token: authenticated user token stripped of gt. prefix when needed.
    • data-theme: current theme preference (dark/light) synchronized with dashboard state.
    • data-vertical: responsive vertical offset (140px on mobile, 80px on desktop).

4. Access Control Verification (src/hooks/useAuth.jsx)

  • Ensure the canAccessChatAI permission flag correctly gates widget script injection and DOM container rendering based on user eligibility.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Production build of the RAG widget bundle (widget.js and widget.css) is placed in public/.
  • Cache-busting version query parameters in Layout.jsx and public/index.html are incremented.
  • Chat widget successfully initializes and opens for authorized users (canAccessChatAI === true).
  • Widget sends chat requests to the new Copilot proxy (POST /copilot/chat) with auth token and conversation context.
  • AI responses with markdown formatting and referenced knowledge sources are displayed correctly.
  • Theme switching (dark/light) reflects properly inside the chat widget.
  • No regressions or console errors in the main layout lifecycle.

Description

Restrict visibility and access to the Professional Services page (/photographer/services) and its navigation elements based on the photographer's role. Only photographers with the image_processing role should have access to this page.

Requirements

1. Sidebar Navigation

  • Show the "Professional Services" menu item in PhotographerMenu and PhotographerNoviceMenu only if the photographer's role is image_processing.
  • Hide this item for all other roles (e.g., photographer_360, image_editor, etc.).

2. Route Guard & Redirection

  • If a user navigates to /photographer/services directly without the image_processing role:
    • Redirect to /photographer/profile if the profile status is approved (status === 3).
    • Redirect to /photographer/submission for novice / unapproved status.
    • Avoid calling the professional services API if the role is unauthorized.

3. Wizard Step Flow

  • In /photographer/tools (Gear & Tools step), clicking Next:
    • Route to /photographer/services if the role is image_processing.
    • Skip directly to /photographer/submission for all other roles.

4. Page Reload State

  • Ensure photographer profile and supporting data are properly initialized on reload so the sidebar does not get stuck in a loading skeleton state.

issues.display_title: Issue #4278: fix(auth): Fix Keycloak callback state mismatch on password reset
issues.main_description_html:
Ref: #4259

Summary

Fix the state_mismatch login failure on /auth/keycloak/callback when returning from a Keycloak password reset.

Problem

When users reset their password via email, the link opens in a new browser tab where sessionStorage (kc_state) is empty. This caused an unintended state mismatch error even though Keycloak returned a valid access token.

Solution

  1. Cross-Tab State: Persist kc_state in both localStorage and sessionStorage.
  2. Graceful Token Exchange: If expectedState is not found in storage (due to email reset links in new tabs), proceed with token exchange to backend where the token is verified cryptographically.
  3. CSRF Protection: Retain strict state matching when expectedState is present in storage.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Standard login via Keycloak continues to validate anti-CSRF state.
  • Password reset links opened in new tabs successfully log in instead of failing with state mismatch.
  • URL hash is immediately stripped on callback.
  • All unit tests pass and build succeeds.

Result

  • PR: Opened via #4277
  • Tests: KeycloakCallback.test.jsx (7/7 tests pass) and Login.countly.test.jsx (3/3 tests pass).
  • Build: Production build verified with npm run build.

Summary

Background

  • Implicit flow hands the Keycloak access token over in the URL fragment (browser-history exposure) and returns no refresh token and no id_token.

issues.display_title: Issue #4291: feat(auth): SSO-aware logout via Keycloak end-session endpoint (post_logout_redirect_uri)
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Make dashboard logout SSO-aware: after calling the GoThru logout API, redirect the browser to the Keycloak end-session endpoint (/protocol/openid-connect/logout) with id_token_hint + post_logout_redirect_uri, so the Keycloak SSO session dies together with the app session.

Background

  • Current logout (Header.jsx handleLogoutAction) only calls POST /v1/auth/logout, clears cookie/localStorage, then redirects to /auth. The Keycloak session is handled server-side via the Admin API, which kills all sessions of that user (every device) — see the related BE issue.
  • The standard OIDC end-session flow is more granular (only the current browser session) and takes the admin credentials out of the FE logout path.
  • Prerequisite from #4290: the login callback now stores the id_token in sessionStorage (kc_id_token) — that token is the id_token_hint.

Tasks

  1. After POST /v1/auth/logout completes (BE session deleted + sid cookie cleared), redirect to:
    {KC_BASE}/realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/logout?id_token_hint=<kc_id_token>&post_logout_redirect_uri={origin}/auth
  2. Only perform step 1 redirect when the user logged in via Keycloak (id_token present in sessionStorage); password/Google logins keep today's behavior (plain redirect to /auth).
  3. Never block the Keycloak redirect if the BE logout call fails; do not rely on post_logout_redirect_uri as the primary way back — Keycloak shows its own default logout page when the URI is unregistered/mismatched.
  4. Clear kc_id_token (and any remaining kc_* context) after logout completes.
  5. Optional: have BE return the pre-built Keycloak logout URL in the logout response so the FE does not need Keycloak config just for logout.

Acceptance

  • SSO user: logout ends the Keycloak session and lands back on /auth
  • SSO user: after logout, starting SSO login again does not silently re-login
  • Password/Google user: logout behaves exactly as today (no Keycloak redirect)
  • BE logout failure still triggers the end-session redirect
  • post_logout_redirect_uri (e.g. https://<host>/auth) registered under the client's Valid post logout redirect URIs (deploy prerequisite)
